name: Discord Cache & Code Cache
whatIsIt: Discord stores a local copy of every video, audio message, GIF, image, and emoji loaded across your servers and direct messages.
whatHappens: Deleting this clears disk space immediately. It does NOT delete your chat history, server memberships, or account credentials. Discord simply re-downloads media as you view it.
manualSteps: Completely exit Discord (right-click the Discord icon in your system tray and select 'Quit Discord').
Press the Windows Key + R to open the Run dialog.
Type %appdata%\discord and hit Enter.
Delete the folders named 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache'.

name: Spotify Offline Storage & Streaming Cache
whatIsIt: Spotify caches streamed song tracks locally on your C: drive to speed up playback and reduce bandwidth usage.
whatHappens: Wiping this cache reclaims several gigabytes. Your playlists and saved songs remain safe in your Spotify account, though downloaded songs for offline mode will need re-syncing.
manualSteps: Close Spotify.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Spotify, and press Enter.
Open the 'Storage' directory, select all files (Ctrl+A), and press Delete.

name: Steam Shader Pre-Caching & Download Bloat
whatIsIt: Steam saves graphics files for every game you play so levels load faster, and those large files stay behind even after you stop playing or uninstall a game.
whatHappens: Completely safe to clean. Your game saves and installed games are never touched.
manualSteps: Open Steam Settings > Downloads.
Scroll to Shader Pre-Caching and review space used.
Navigate to C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\shadercache and delete old game app-id folders.

name: Google Chrome Service Worker & CacheStorage
whatIsIt: Websites you visit in Chrome (like YouTube, Gmail, and online tools) quietly store gigabytes of offline files on your hard drive.
whatHappens: Frees up hidden browser storage right away. You stay signed in to your accounts and nothing important is lost.
manualSteps: Close Google Chrome.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default and hit Enter.
Locate 'Service Worker' and delete the 'CacheStorage' directory.

name: Windows WinSxS Component Store (C:\Windows\WinSxS)
warning: Never delete C:\Windows\WinSxS manually in File Explorer—doing so will break Windows boot and system servicing. Always clean WinSxS via DISM or SWEEPR Cleaner.
whatIsIt: C:\Windows\WinSxS (Windows Side-by-Side Component Store) contains the master files for every Windows 10 and Windows 11 system component, cumulative update rollback package, and optional feature. While many files appear large due to NTFS hard links, superseded Windows Update packages genuinely consume 6 GB to 20 GB+ of physical disk space.
whatHappens: Running a safe Component Store cleanup removes superseded Windows Update versions and Temp\PendingRenames staging files, freeing 6 GB – 20 GB on your C: drive with zero risk to Windows stability.
manualSteps: Open Command Prompt or PowerShell as Administrator (Win + X -> Terminal (Admin)).
First check reclaimable space by running: Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore
If Component Store Cleanup Recommended says Yes, run: Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup
Or run SWEEPR Cleaner to automate DISM Component Store pruning alongside 40+ other hidden Windows folders in one click.

name: Windows System Temp Folder
whatIsIt: Old setup files and temporary logs created by Windows updates and installers that are no longer needed.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete. Any file currently being used by Windows is automatically skipped.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\Temp and press Enter (click Continue if prompted for administrator access).
Select all items with Ctrl+A and press Shift+Delete.
Check 'Do this for all current items' and click Skip if a file is currently in use.

name: User AppData Local Temp Directory
whatIsIt: Apps use this folder as a scratchpad for temporary files when opening downloads or installing updates, and often forget to clean it up.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees up gigabytes of wasted space immediately while skipping any files currently open.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %temp% and press Enter.
Select all files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.
If Windows prompts that a file is open in another program, check 'Do this for all current items' and choose Skip.

name: Windows.old (Previous Windows Installation)
whatIsIt: When Windows upgrades to a major new version or build, it saves a complete backup of your previous OS files in C:\Windows.old so you can roll back.
whatHappens: If your PC has been running smoothly for more than 10 days after an update, deleting Windows.old is completely safe and reclaims 20+ GB.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage.
Click on 'Temporary files'.
Check 'Previous Windows installation(s)' and click 'Remove files'.

name: pnpm Content-Addressable Store & Metadata Cache
whatIsIt: pnpm caches registry metadata and unreferenced package blobs from deleted JavaScript repositories.

Delete %localappdata%\pnpm-cache to clear stale registry metadata.

name: Yarn Global Package Cache (%LocalAppData%\Yarn\Cache)
whatIsIt: Yarn caches zip archives of every downloaded npm dependency in %LocalAppData%\Yarn\Cache.

name: Rust Cargo Registry Crate & Git Cache (.cargo\registry)
whatIsIt: Rust's Cargo package manager keeps every downloaded .crate archive and unpacked source tree in %UserProfile%\.cargo\registry.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Your installed cargo binaries (.cargo\bin) and rustup toolchains are untouched.

Delete the 'cache' and 'src' folders.

name: Python pip Wheel & HTTP Download Cache
whatIsIt: Python's pip installer caches large AI/ML wheels (PyTorch, CUDA, TensorFlow, NumPy) in %LocalAppData%\pip\Cache.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Virtual environments (venv/conda) and installed Python packages are not affected.
manualSteps: Run 'pip cache purge' in Command Prompt or PowerShell.
Or navigate to %localappdata%\pip\Cache and delete all files.

name: .NET NuGet HTTP & Temp Cache
whatIsIt: Visual Studio and the .NET SDK cache downloaded NuGet HTTP responses and scratch packages in %LocalAppData%\NuGet.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims gigabytes of SSD space; Visual Studio automatically restores any needed package on build.

name: Gradle Build Cache & Wrapper Distributions (.gradle\caches)
whatIsIt: Android Studio and Java/Kotlin builds accumulate multiple gigabytes of old Gradle wrapper versions, build caches, and daemon logs in .gradle.
whatHappens: Safe to clean when Android Studio/IntelliJ is closed. Reclaims up to 35 GB of SSD space.

Delete old daemon logs and unused transform caches inside .gradle\caches.

name: JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, RustRover) Caches
whatIsIt: JetBrains IDEs store huge local history indexes, AST caches, and old IDE version folders inside %LocalAppData%\JetBrains.

name: Android SDK System Image Download Intermediates
whatIsIt: The Android SDK Manager leaves multi-gigabyte zip archives in .temp and .downloadIntermediates after installing system images or NDKs.

whatIsIt: Docker Desktop on Windows 11 accumulates dangling container layers, BuildKit caches, and verbose host logs in %LocalAppData%\Docker.

whatIsIt: PHP's Composer dependency manager caches downloaded zip packages and Packagist JSON metadata in %LocalAppData%\Composer.

name: Postman Desktop Logs & Chromium Cache

name: 7-Zip & WinRAR Orphaned Archive Extraction Temp (7zO* / Rar$*)

Delete all folders starting with '7z' or 'Rar$'.

name: Plex Media Server Transcode & PhotoTranscoder Cache

Delete the contents of 'PhotoTranscoder' and 'Transcode'.

name: Grammarly for Windows Logs & WebView Cache
whatIsIt: Grammarly's Windows overlay writes daily diagnostic logs and WebView caches in %LocalAppData%\Grammarly.

Navigate to %localappdata%\Grammarly and delete old log files.

Delete 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache'.

whatIsIt: Is LGHUB cache safe to delete? Logitech G HUB downloads compressed firmware and software update depots into C:\ProgramData\LGHUB\depots and stores Chromium UI media blobs in %LocalAppData%\LGHUB. Old depot folders are frequently left behind after updates.

Check 'Delivery Optimization Files'.
Click 'Remove files' at the top.

whatIsIt: Windows tracks how applications start up in .pf trace files inside C:\Windows\Prefetch, including hundreds of dead traces from uninstalled programs.
whatHappens: Safe to purge periodically when cluttered with old uninstalled app traces; Windows automatically rebuilds fresh traces for your current apps.

manualSteps: Right-click Start and open Terminal (Admin).
To shrink hiberfil.sys by 50% while keeping Fast Startup, run: powercfg /h /type reduced.
To remove hiberfil.sys completely, run: powercfg /h off.

name: Windows Virtual Memory Pagefile (C:\pagefile.sys)
warning: Never force-delete pagefile.sys. It is actively used by the Windows kernel as virtual memory overflow.

whatHappens: Instead of deleting pagefile.sys, clean surrounding cache folders with SWEEPR Cleaner or cap its maximum size in Advanced System Settings if it has ballooned unnecessarily.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type sysdm.cpl and press Enter.
Go to Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual Memory > Change.
Keep a system-managed pagefile on your fastest SSD, or move it to a secondary NVMe drive if C: is critically full.

name: Windows Modern UWP Swapfile (C:\swapfile.sys)
warning: Managed automatically by the Windows memory manager alongside pagefile.sys.
whatIsIt: A small 256 MB dedicated swap file used by Windows 10/11 to suspend and resume Microsoft Store (UWP) apps in the background.
whatHappens: Managed automatically by Windows; focus on cleaning UWP app LocalCache folders instead.
manualSteps: Leave C:\swapfile.sys managed by Windows.
To reclaim space from UWP apps, scan %LocalAppData%\Packages with SWEEPR Cleaner.

name: System Volume Information (VSS Shadow Copies & Restore Points)
warning: Do not modify permissions or delete files inside System Volume Information manually. Use Windows System Protection or vssadmin to prune old restore points.
whatIsIt: Stores Windows System Restore points and Volume Shadow Copy snapshots on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Deleting older superseded restore points while keeping your most recent restore point safely reclaims 10–40 GB.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type sysdm.cpl and press Enter.
Open the 'System Protection' tab, select Local Disk (C:), and click 'Configure'.
Adjust the Max Usage slider (e.g., to 5%) or click 'Delete' to clear outdated restore points.

name: $Windows.~BT & $Windows.~WS Hidden Upgrade Staging Folders
whatIsIt: Hidden root folders created by the Windows 11 Installation Assistant and Media Creation Tool during feature upgrades.
whatHappens: Once your Windows upgrade has finished, deleting $Windows.~BT and $Windows.~WS is 100% safe and reclaims up to 18 GB.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Windows upgrade log files' and 'Temporary Windows installation files'.
Click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Error Reporting (WER) ReportArchive & ReportQueue
whatIsIt: Whenever an application or service crashes on Windows, WER writes diagnostic archives and heap snapshots into ReportArchive and ReportQueue.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees up gigabytes of old crash diagnostic logs.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WER and press Enter.
Delete the contents of 'ReportArchive', 'ReportQueue', and 'Temp'.

name: User Application CrashDumps (%LocalAppData%\CrashDumps)
whatIsIt: Windows WER writes full process memory dumps (.dmp) into %LocalAppData%\CrashDumps whenever a game or desktop app crashes.
whatHappens: Completely safe to delete unless you are actively debugging a recent crash in WinDbg.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\CrashDumps and press Enter.
Select all .dmp files (Ctrl+A) and press Delete.

name: Kernel Memory Dump & Minidump (C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP & Minidump)
whatIsIt: If your PC ever experienced a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD), Windows writes a massive kernel memory dump to C:\Windows\MEMORY.DMP.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete once your system is stable, reclaiming up to 16 GB from a single file.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'System error memory dump files' and 'System error minidump files'.
Click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows File Explorer Thumbnail & Icon Cache (thumbcache_*.db)
whatIsIt: File Explorer caches image, video, and document thumbnails in thumbcache_*.db and iconcache_*.db files that grow continuously over time.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Fixes blank/broken desktop icons and frees up disk space; Windows regenerates thumbnails for active folders on demand.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Thumbnails' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Microsoft DirectX D3DSCache Shader Cache
whatIsIt: Windows' built-in Direct3D shader cache used by DirectX 12 games, browsers, and desktop UI effects.
whatHappens: 100% safe to clean. Removes stale shaders and resolves graphical glitches after Windows updates.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'DirectX Shader Cache' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Component-Based Servicing Logs (C:\Windows\Logs\CBS)
whatIsIt: The Windows Module Installer (TiWorker.exe) writes massive text and .cab archives to C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log and CbsPersist_*.cab.
whatHappens: Deleting old CbsPersist_*.log and .cab files is completely safe and reclaims gigabytes on older Windows installations.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\Logs\CBS and press Enter (as Admin).
Delete old CbsPersist_*.cab and .log files (skip the currently open CBS.log).

name: DISM & SetupAPI Diagnostic Logs (C:\Windows\Logs\DISM)
whatIsIt: Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM) and driver installations append diagnostic logs in C:\Windows\Logs.
whatHappens: Safe to clean old archive logs to free C: drive space.
manualSteps: Navigate to C:\Windows\Logs\DISM.
Delete archived dism.log.bak files.

name: Windows Setup Panther Upgrade Logs (C:\Windows\Panther)
whatIsIt: Contains diagnostic ETL traces and setupact.log files generated during Windows installation and feature upgrades.
whatHappens: Cleaning old setup log files via Storage Sense / SWEEPR Cleaner safely reclaims disk space.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Windows upgrade log files' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows LiveKernelReports & WATCHDOG GPU Crash Dumps (C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports)
whatIsIt: What is C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports? Whenever your NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel graphics driver experiences a brief Timeout Detection and Recovery (TDR) freeze (Event ID 4101) without a full blue screen, Windows writes a huge uncompressed kernel memory dump (WATCHDOG-*.dmp, often 500 MB to 2 GB each) into C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports.
whatHappens: Yes, C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports is 100% safe to delete. Removing old WATCHDOG and PoW32kWatchdog .dmp files reclaims 1.5 GB – 10.0 GB immediately with zero impact on Windows or your GPU drivers.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports and press Enter (click Continue if prompted for Administrator permission).
Open the WATCHDOG subfolder and any sibling folders, select all .dmp files, and press Shift + Delete.
Alternatively, run Disk Cleanup as Administrator or use SWEEPR Cleaner to purge all kernel and user-mode crash dumps in 1 click.

name: Microsoft Office Legacy Local Installation Source (C:\MSOCache)
whatIsIt: Older Microsoft Office MSI installations create a hidden C:\MSOCache folder containing cached cabinet (.cab) setup files.
whatHappens: Can be safely cleaned via Disk Cleanup ('Office Setup Files') once you are on modern Microsoft 365 Click-to-Run.
manualSteps: Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) as Administrator.
Check 'Office Setup Files' if present and click OK.

name: Windows INetCache (Legacy Temporary Internet Files & WebView Cache)
whatIsIt: Desktop applications using the Windows WinINet API cache downloaded installers, RSS feeds, and web assets in %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete. Frees disk space used by background desktop updaters.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Temporary Internet Files' and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Font Cache (FontCache-S-*.dat)
whatIsIt: Windows caches rendered glyph outlines for all installed system and Adobe/Figma fonts inside the LocalService FontCache directory.
whatHappens: Safe to rebuild when bloated or corrupted; fixes garbled font rendering in Windows apps.
manualSteps: Stop the 'Windows Font Cache Service' (FontCache) in services.msc.
Delete the FontCache*.dat files inside C:\Windows\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\FontCache, then restart the service.

name: Windows Certificate CRL & OCSP URL Cache (CryptnetUrlCache)
whatIsIt: Windows caches downloaded SSL certificate revocation lists (CRLs) and Authenticode OCSP responses in CryptnetUrlCache.
whatHappens: Safe to clear; Windows automatically fetches fresh certificate revocation data when verifying signed apps.
manualSteps: Open Command Prompt and run: certutil -urlcache * delete.
This safely flushes stale CryptnetUrlCache entries.

name: Windows System Resource Usage Monitor (C:\Windows\System32\sru)
whatIsIt: Windows logs 30–60 days of per-process network, CPU, and energy usage telemetry into SRUDB.dat inside System32\sru.
whatHappens: Resetting a bloated SRUDB.dat file reclaims space and only clears historical 30-day App History graphs in Task Manager.
manualSteps: Open Task Manager > App history and click 'Delete usage history'.

name: Windows DriverStore Superseded GPU & Audio Driver Packages
warning: Never delete folders inside FileRepository manually in File Explorer. Always use pnputil /delete-driver or Windows Storage Sense ('Device driver packages').
whatIsIt: Every time NVIDIA, AMD, or Windows Update installs a new graphics or audio driver, the old 800MB driver package remains in DriverStore\FileRepository.
whatHappens: Cleaning superseded driver packages via pnputil or Storage Sense safely reclaims 5–25 GB without affecting your current active driver.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'Device driver packages' and click 'Remove files'.
Advanced users can list unused drivers with: pnputil /enum-drivers.

name: Hidden $Recycle.Bin Corrupted & Per-Drive Trash
whatIsIt: Each NTFS drive maintains a hidden $Recycle.Bin folder partitioned by user SID, which can retain gigabytes of deleted files across multiple accounts.
whatHappens: 100% safe to empty once you have verified you no longer need any deleted files in the Recycle Bin.
manualSteps: Right-click the Recycle Bin on your Desktop and select 'Empty Recycle Bin'.
If corrupted, run in Admin Command Prompt: rd /s /q C:\$Recycle.Bin (Windows recreates a clean folder automatically).

name: Windows Store UWP Apps TempState & AC\Temp (%LocalAppData%\Packages)
whatIsIt: Every Microsoft Store app (Photos, Clipchamp, Xbox, WhatsApp, Paint) has its own sandboxed TempState and AC\Temp directory inside %LocalAppData%\Packages.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete TempState and AC\Temp contents across all UWP packages without resetting app logins.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Packages and press Enter.
Clean the 'TempState' and 'AC\Temp' subfolders inside heavy UWP apps, or run SWEEPR Cleaner to scan all UWP sandboxes at once.

name: Microsoft Clipchamp Video Editor EBWebView & Media Cache
whatIsIt: Windows 11's built-in Clipchamp video editor caches multi-gigabyte video buffers and WebView2 blobs inside its UWP LocalCache.
whatHappens: Safe to clear once your exported MP4 video is saved to your Videos folder.
manualSteps: Open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Microsoft Clipchamp > Advanced options.
Click 'Reset' after exporting your completed videos, or clean its LocalCache\EBWebView folder.

name: Windows RetailDemo Offline Content Bloat
whatIsIt: Pre-installed store display demo assets shipped on retail Windows 10 and Windows 11 installations.
whatHappens: 100% safe to remove on any personal or work PC.
manualSteps: Open Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
Check 'RetailDemo Offline Content' if listed and click 'Remove files'.

name: Windows Downloaded Program Files & Legacy ActiveX Cache
whatIsIt: Legacy staging folder used by old web controls and enterprise installers.
whatHappens: Safe to clean via Disk Cleanup or SWEEPR Cleaner.
manualSteps: Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe).
Check 'Downloaded Program Files' and click OK.

name: Windows BranchCache Peer Caching Directory
whatIsIt: Enterprise and Windows Pro network cache used to store shared intranet and update payloads.
whatHappens: Safe to flush via netsh branchcache flush or Disk Cleanup.
manualSteps: Open Terminal (Admin) and run: netsh branchcache flush.
This immediately clears all cached BranchCache files.

name: Microsoft Defender Expired Quarantine Items
whatIsIt: Holds neutralized threats and PUA installers quarantined by Microsoft Defender.
whatHappens: Purging old quarantined threats permanently deletes neutralized files and frees disk space.
manualSteps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history.
Select Quarantined items and click 'Remove' to permanently delete them.

name: Bloated Windows Search Index Database (Windows.edb)
warning: Rebuild the index via Indexing Options rather than deleting Windows.edb while SearchIndexer.exe is running.
whatIsIt: The Windows Search service indexes file contents and Outlook mail into Windows.edb, which can fragment and bloat to 15–25 GB over time.
whatHappens: Rebuilding the index compacts Windows.edb back down to a fraction of its size without losing any user files.
manualSteps: Open Control Panel > Indexing Options > Advanced.
Under Troubleshooting, click 'Rebuild' to compact and recreate a clean search index.

name: WSL2 Linux Virtual Disk Bloat (ext4.vhdx)
warning: Never delete ext4.vhdx directly or you will erase your Linux distribution! Clean /tmp and apt cache inside WSL, then compact the virtual disk.
whatIsIt: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2) dynamically expands ext4.vhdx as you download files in Linux, but does not automatically shrink it when you delete them.
whatHappens: Cleaning Linux caches and running 'wsl --manage <distro> --set-sparse true' or diskpart compact vdisk safely reclaims tens of gigabytes on Windows.
manualSteps: Inside WSL, run: sudo apt-get clean && sudo rm -rf /tmp/*.
In Windows PowerShell, run: wsl --shutdown.
Compact the virtual disk or use SWEEPR Cleaner to clear surrounding Windows host caches.

name: Leftover NVIDIA Driver Unpack Directory (C:\NVIDIA)
whatIsIt: When you run standalone NVIDIA GeForce driver installers, they extract uncompressed setup files into C:\NVIDIA\DisplayDriver before installing.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after the driver installation is complete! Your installed NVIDIA driver lives in C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore, not C:\NVIDIA.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer and navigate to Local Disk (C:).
If a folder named C:\NVIDIA exists, right-click it and select Delete.

name: Leftover AMD Radeon Driver Unpack Directory (C:\AMD)
whatIsIt: AMD Radeon Adrenalin and Chipset installers extract their uncompressed setup packages into C:\AMD for every version you've ever installed.
whatHappens: 100% safe to delete after driver installation finishes! Your installed AMD drivers are already copied to C:\Program Files\AMD and System32.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer and navigate to C:\AMD.
Delete all old version subfolders inside C:\AMD to reclaim up to 12 GB instantly.

name: Windows SleepStudy & Energy Diagnostic ETL Traces
whatIsIt: Windows records continuous Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) power and Modern Standby sessions in C:\Windows\System32\SleepStudy.
whatHappens: Old historical .etl traces in SleepStudy\ScreenOnPowerStudyTraceSession can be safely purged.
manualSteps: Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\SleepStudy as Administrator.
Remove old archived .etl trace files.

name: Ollama Local LLM Models & Orphaned Blob Cache
whatIsIt: Ollama stores quantized GGUF large language model weights and orphaned layer blobs from interrupted pulls or old model versions on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Removing unused model blobs frees massive SSD space immediately. Models you still use can be re-pulled anytime with 'ollama pull'.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal and run 'ollama list' to inspect installed local models.
Remove unused models with 'ollama rm <model-name>', or quit the Ollama tray app.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.ollama\models\blobs, and delete orphaned blob files.

name: LM Studio GGUF Model Cache & Temp Downloads
whatIsIt: LM Studio downloads multi-gigabyte HuggingFace GGUF model checkpoints and temporary partial downloads into your user cache folder.
whatHappens: Deleting unused model folders reclaims tens of gigabytes of SSD space without affecting your LM Studio presets or chat history.
manualSteps: Close LM Studio completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.cache\lm-studio\models, and press Enter.
Delete any publisher/model folders you no longer actively run.

name: HuggingFace Hub Transformers & Diffusers Cache
whatIsIt: Python AI tools, Diffusers, and Transformers cache every downloaded safetensors checkpoint and tokenizer snapshot inside .cache\huggingface\hub.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims disk space from old model revisions and unused AI weights. Active Python scripts will automatically re-download only what they need.
manualSteps: Close any running Python or AI generation terminals.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\.cache\huggingface\hub, and press Enter.
Delete old 'models--*' directories or temp download lock files.

name: ComfyUI Temporary Preview & Latent Cache
whatIsIt: ComfyUI writes uncompressed PNG step previews, intermediate workflow latents, and video frame sequences during image and video generation.
whatHappens: Clears temporary generation clutter without touching your saved workflows, custom nodes, or final output images.
manualSteps: Stop the ComfyUI server process.
Open your ComfyUI installation folder and navigate to the 'temp' subfolder.
Select all temporary preview files (Ctrl+A) and delete them.

name: PyTorch Torch Hub & CUDA Inductors Cache
whatIsIt: PyTorch caches compiled Triton/CUDA kernels, TorchVision pretrained weights, and C++ extension build artifacts.
whatHappens: Reclaims gigabytes of SSD space. PyTorch simply recompiles active kernels on the next run.
manualSteps: Close active Python processes.
Open %userprofile%\.cache\torch\hub\checkpoints in File Explorer.
Delete old .pth and .pt weight files that are no longer needed.

name: Cursor AI Code Editor Cache & Codebase Index Bloat
whatIsIt: Cursor stores Chromium GPU caches, V8 bytecode snapshots, and old VSIX extension installers in your Roaming AppData folder.
whatHappens: Frees up several gigabytes of C: drive space while keeping all your extensions, keybindings, and AI settings intact.
manualSteps: Close Cursor completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\Cursor, and press Enter.
Delete the 'Cache', 'CachedData', 'CachedExtensionVSIXs', and 'GPUCache' folders.

name: Unity Global Illumination (GI) & Asset Store Cache
whatIsIt: Unity Editor caches baked Global Illumination lighting data, UPM package tarballs, and downloaded Asset Store packages on your system drive.
whatHappens: Reclaims gigabytes of SSD space without modifying your Unity project scenes, scripts, or prefabs.
manualSteps: Close Unity Editor and Unity Hub.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Unity\cache\packages and %localappdata%\Unity\cache\npm.
Delete old cached package folders to reclaim space.

name: Call of Duty HQ & Warzone Pre-Compiled Shader Cache
whatIsIt: Call of Duty HQ and Warzone store multi-gigabyte DirectX 12 shader packs that grow after every seasonal update and GPU driver change.
whatHappens: Frees disk space and fixes post-update stuttering or packet-burst hitching by forcing a clean shader optimization on next launch.
manualSteps: Exit Call of Duty completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Activision\Call of Duty\shadercache, and hit Enter.
Delete all files inside the shadercache directory.

name: Fortnite DirectX 12 Pipeline & Cosmetics Stream Cache
whatIsIt: Fortnite caches streamed high-resolution cosmetic textures, replay recordings, crash dumps, and DirectX 12 PSO shader caches.
whatHappens: Reclaims wasted C: drive space and resolves DX12 shader stutter without affecting your Epic account or keybinds.
manualSteps: Close Fortnite and Epic Games Launcher.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\FortniteGame\Saved, and press Enter.
Clear the 'Logs', 'Crashes', and old 'Demos' replay files.

name: VRChat Downloaded World & Avatar Cache
whatIsIt: VRChat downloads every custom 3D world and user avatar you encounter into LocalLow\VRChat, rapidly consuming 20GB+ on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Immediately frees 10–30 GB of SSD space. VRChat will only re-download worlds and avatars you visit in future sessions.
manualSteps: Exit VRChat.
Press Windows Key + R, type %userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\VRChat\VRChat\Cache-WindowsPlayer, and hit Enter.
Select all cached folders and delete them.

name: FiveM GTA V Server Asset & Priv Cache
whatIsIt: FiveM caches custom vehicles, MLO interiors, clothing packs, and scripts from every RP server you have ever joined.
whatHappens: Frees tens of gigabytes of SSD space and fixes FiveM texture loss or crash-on-join issues.
manualSteps: Close FiveM.
Open %localappdata%\FiveM\FiveM.app\data in File Explorer.
Delete the 'cache', 'server-cache', and 'server-cache-priv' folders (do NOT delete 'game-storage').

name: Windows 11 24H2 Cumulative Checkpoint Update Cache
whatIsIt: Windows 11 24H2 stores differential checkpoint update payloads and uncompressed cab/msu staging files in SoftwareDistribution\Download.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims gigabytes of C: drive space after updates finish installing and resolves stuck Windows Update error codes.
manualSteps: Open Terminal (Admin) and run: net stop wuauserv
Open C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\Download and delete all files inside.
Restart the Windows Update service with: net start wuauserv

name: Windows ProgramData Package Cache (C:\ProgramData\Package Cache)
warning: Do NOT blindly delete the entire C:\ProgramData\Package Cache folder in File Explorer—removing active Wix/Burn .msi caches can prevent Visual C++ Redistributables or Visual Studio from repairing or uninstalling.
whatIsIt: C:\ProgramData\Package Cache is used by the Windows WiX Burn bootstrapper to store cached .msi and .cab installer baselines for Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables, .NET runtimes, Visual Studio, and third-party drivers. Over years of updates, dozens of superseded versions accumulate.
whatHappens: Pruning only orphaned and superseded package cache GUID folders reclaims 3.5 GB – 22.0 GB of C: drive space while keeping active uninstaller baselines healthy.
manualSteps: Never select all folders inside C:\ProgramData\Package Cache and hit Delete—active applications rely on their registered GUID folder to run Modify/Repair/Uninstall.
Open Settings > Apps > Installed Apps first and uninstall any old SDKs or Visual Studio workloads you no longer need.
To safely clean only orphaned GUID folders whose parent product is already uninstalled, run SWEEPR Cleaner’s verified Package Cache orphan scanner.

name: Windows DriverStore Temp & Superseded OEM Packages
whatIsIt: Windows stages extracted GPU, chipset, and audio driver packages in DriverStore\Temp during device installation and Windows Update.
whatHappens: Deleting leftover staging files in DriverStore\Temp frees C: drive space without affecting your currently active hardware drivers.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal as Administrator.
Run 'pnputil /enum-drivers' to inspect installed third-party OEM driver packages.
Clear C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\Temp or use SWEEPR Cleaner to safely purge superseded driver staging files.

name: SquirrelTemp Leftover App Update Packages (%LocalAppData%\SquirrelTemp)
whatIsIt: Desktop apps built with Squirrel (Discord, Slack, Postman, Teams, WhatsApp) leave behind full .nupkg installer packages in SquirrelTemp.
whatHappens: Safely deletes leftover update installers without affecting the installed applications.
manualSteps: Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\SquirrelTemp, and press Enter.
Delete all temporary .nupkg packages and staging folders.

name: Microsoft Edge WebView2 Shared Runtime Cache (EBWebView)
whatIsIt: Windows 11 widgets, Microsoft 365 apps, and modern desktop utilities embed Edge WebView2, accumulating gigabytes of cached web data.
whatHappens: Reclaims hidden SSD space while keeping Windows Widgets and Office add-ins working normally.
manualSteps: Close Widgets and Office apps.
Navigate to %localappdata%\Microsoft\EdgeWebView\User Data\Default.
Delete the 'Cache', 'Code Cache', and 'GPUCache' folders.

name: Microsoft Defender Protection & Scan History Cache
whatIsIt: Microsoft Defender Antivirus logs historical scan results and quarantined detection metadata inside ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender.
whatHappens: Clears old detection history logs and reclaims disk space while keeping real-time antivirus protection active.
manualSteps: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history.
Or use SWEEPR Cleaner to clear expired scan log caches older than 30 days.

name: Windows Desktop Icon Cache Database (IconCache.db)
whatIsIt: Windows caches desktop, Start Menu, and taskbar shortcut icons inside the hidden IconCache.db file in %LocalAppData%.
whatHappens: Safe to delete. Frees disk space and forces Windows Explorer to rebuild a fresh icon cache, fixing corrupted, generic blank sheet, or missing desktop icons.
manualSteps: Close open applications and open Terminal as Administrator.
Stop Windows Explorer with: taskkill /f /im explorer.exe
Delete the icon cache database: del /f /q %LocalAppData%\IconCache.db
Restart Windows Explorer: start explorer.exe

name: Git Large File Storage (LFS) Objects Cache
whatIsIt: Git LFS keeps local copies of binary assets, textures, and 3D models even after you switch branches or delete files.
whatHappens: Safely prunes unreferenced Git LFS media blobs while keeping your remote repositories fully intact.
manualSteps: Open Terminal in your Git repository.
Run: git lfs prune to safely discard unreferenced binary files.
Clear old Git credential and clone cache directories in %localappdata%.

name: Rustup Toolchain Downloads & Old Component Temp
whatIsIt: Rustup downloads compressed toolchain tarballs (rustc, cargo, rust-docs) and keeps leftover archives in downloads.
whatHappens: Deleting leftover archives reclaims SSD space without altering your installed Rust toolchains.
manualSteps: Open %userprofile%\.rustup in File Explorer.
Select and delete all files inside the 'downloads' directory.
Run 'rustup check' to verify toolchain integrity.

name: AMD Radeon Software OpenGL Shader Cache
whatIsIt: AMD graphics drivers compile and store OpenGL and Vulkan pipeline binary shaders in %LocalAppData%\AMD\OglCache.
whatHappens: Reclaims disk space and forces games to rebuild clean shader binaries on next run.
manualSteps: Quit running 3D emulators and OpenGL games.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\AMD\OglCache, and hit Enter.
Select all files (Ctrl+A) and delete them.

name: Windows Event Viewer Historical Logs (winevt\Logs)
whatIsIt: Windows writes Application, System, Security, and Diagnostic event logs into multi-megabyte .evtx binary log files.
whatHappens: Safely clears bloated event log archives when disk space is critically low.
manualSteps: Open Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc).
Right-click 'Application' or 'System' and select 'Clear Log'.
Or use SWEEPR Cleaner to safely archive and purge old Windows event logs in 1 click.

name: Windows Prefetch ReadyBoot Trace Files (ReadyBoot)
whatIsIt: Windows generates boot prefetch trace files in C:\Windows\Prefetch\ReadyBoot to monitor system startup sequences.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up stale boot trace files without altering your system boot configuration.
manualSteps: Open Terminal as Administrator.
Navigate to C:\Windows\Prefetch\ReadyBoot.
Delete old .fx trace files.

name: Bun JavaScript Runtime Package & Install Cache
whatIsIt: Bun caches downloaded npm packages, binary tarballs, and compiled native bindings in .bun\install\cache for ultra-fast offline installs.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up stale package downloads and frees gigabytes of SSD space. Bun will re-fetch only needed packages on subsequent install commands.
manualSteps: Open Windows Terminal.
Run 'bun pm cache rm' to purge the global package cache.
Or delete the %userprofile%\.bun\install\cache directory in File Explorer.

name: Conda & Anaconda Package Tarball Cache (%UserProfile%\.conda\pkgs)
whatIsIt: Conda and Anaconda download compressed conda package archives (.conda and .tar.bz2) and unpack them into pkgs before linking into environments.
whatHappens: Safely deletes unlinked package archives, cache tarballs, and temporary downloads without corrupting existing virtual environments.
manualSteps: Open Anaconda Prompt or Windows Terminal.
Run 'conda clean --all -y' to purge all unused packages and tarballs.
Verify reclaimed disk space in %userprofile%\.conda\pkgs.

name: Rust Cargo Package Index & Crate Source Cache
whatIsIt: The Cargo package manager caches crates.io index snapshots, git checkouts, and downloaded .crate archive files in your user profile.
whatHappens: Reclaims gigabytes of C: drive space from old crate versions. Active projects automatically redownload required crates during cargo build.
manualSteps: Close any active IDE or terminal compiling Rust code.
Open %userprofile%\.cargo\registry in File Explorer.
Delete the 'cache' and 'src' folders to free space, or run 'cargo clean' inside project folders.

name: Unity Engine Local Shader Compilation Cache
whatIsIt: Unity compiles and caches HLSL and ShaderLab shader variants across every project you develop into %LocalAppData%\Unity\cache\shaders.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up stale compiled shader binaries and reclaims SSD storage. Unity automatically recompiles active shaders on demand.
manualSteps: Close Unity Editor and Unity Hub.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Unity\cache\shaders, and press Enter.
Select all cached shader directories and delete them.

name: Godot Engine Editor Data & Export Templates Cache
whatIsIt: Godot Engine caches imported texture thumbnails, script documentation indexes, and old export template packages on your system drive.
whatHappens: Reclaims gigabytes of disk space without affecting your project source files or project.godot configuration.
manualSteps: Close the Godot Engine editor.
Open %appdata%\Godot in File Explorer.
Delete the 'editor_data' and 'tmp' subfolders to clear stale cache files.

name: Adobe Substance 3D Painter Shelf & Texture Cache
whatIsIt: Substance 3D Painter caches high-resolution texture mipmaps, baked normal maps, and brush shelf thumbnails in AppData.
whatHappens: Frees significant SSD space and resolves texture viewport corruption without modifying your .spp project files.
manualSteps: Exit Adobe Substance 3D Painter.
Navigate to %appdata%\Adobe\Adobe Substance 3D Painter\cache in File Explorer.
Delete cached mipmaps and temporary thumbnail folders.

name: CurseForge Mod & Addon Download Archive Cache
whatIsIt: CurseForge keeps zip archives of downloaded World of Warcraft addons, Minecraft modpacks, and Sims 4 custom content in its download cache.
whatHappens: Frees gigabytes of storage from previously installed zip archives without removing active mods from your games.
manualSteps: Close the CurseForge app.
Navigate to %userprofile%\CurseForge\Cache in File Explorer.
Delete downloaded archive files to recover drive space.

name: Mod Organizer 2 Staged Archive & Download Cache
whatIsIt: Mod Organizer 2 retains 7z and zip mod installer archives after mods have already been extracted and installed into your profile.
whatHappens: Safely reclaims tens of gigabytes of disk space once your mod load order is verified and operational.
manualSteps: Open Mod Organizer 2 and confirm all installed mods work properly.
Right-click downloaded archives in the Downloads tab and delete them, or delete files directly in %localappdata%\ModOrganizer\downloads.

name: Nexus Mods Vortex Archive Staging & Download Cache
whatIsIt: Vortex retains multi-gigabyte Nexus Mods zip/7z archives in its download directory even after deployment via hard links.
whatHappens: Deleting installed archives frees massive SSD space without affecting hard-linked mods in your game folders.
manualSteps: Open Vortex Mod Manager.
Navigate to the Downloads tab.
Remove completed archives that have already been installed.

name: EA AntiCheat Service Logs & Crash Dump Dumps
whatIsIt: The EA AntiCheat background driver and client write verbose telemetry traces and memory dump files during game launches (EA FC, Battlefield).
whatHappens: Safely deletes stale diagnostic log clutter and frees disk space without interfering with EA game anti-cheat verification.
manualSteps: Close EA App and all EA games.
Open C:\ProgramData\EA Desktop in File Explorer.
Delete old log files and dump files inside the EA AntiCheat folder.

name: Riot Vanguard Kernel Driver Logs & Crash Memory Dumps
whatIsIt: Riot Vanguard creates kernel driver execution logs, memory snapshots, and watchdog trace files during Valorant and League of Legends matches.
whatHappens: Safely purges historical diagnostic text logs and dump files without affecting the active Vanguard anti-cheat kernel service.
manualSteps: Exit Valorant and League of Legends.
Open C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard\Logs in File Explorer as Administrator.
Delete old .log and .dmp files.

name: Easy Anti-Cheat Diagnostic Logs & Certificate Cache
whatIsIt: Easy Anti-Cheat accumulates game crash reports, error traces, and cached security certificates across titles like Apex Legends and Fortnite.
whatHappens: Clears old error trace clutter and fixes anti-cheat initialization loop errors without uninstalling games.
manualSteps: Exit any running games protected by Easy Anti-Cheat.
Press Windows Key + R, type %appdata%\EasyAntiCheat, and press Enter.
Delete old .log files.

name: Windows Xbox App Cloud Gaming & Install Temp Cache
whatIsIt: The Windows 11 Xbox App caches cloud gaming stream chunks, game pass cover art, and interrupted game installation blobs in LocalCache.
whatHappens: Safely frees gigabytes of storage and fixes stuck Xbox Game Pass game download or update errors.
manualSteps: Close the Xbox App and terminate GamingServices in Task Manager.
Open %localappdata%\Packages\Microsoft.GamingApp_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalCache.
Select and delete all cached temporary files.

name: Windows Bluetooth Pairing Logs & Diagnostic Traces
whatIsIt: Windows logs Bluetooth LE connection attempts, RFCOMM socket events, and audio packet drops into dedicated event log files.
whatHappens: Clearing historical Bluetooth logs frees drive space without unpairing any of your connected wireless devices.
manualSteps: Open Windows Event Viewer as Administrator.
Navigate to Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Bluetooth.
Right-click operational logs and select 'Clear Log'.

name: Windows Diagnostic Data & Telemetry ETL Log Queue
whatIsIt: The Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service collects system performance traces (.etl files) before uploading them to Microsoft servers.
whatHappens: Deleting queued ETL files frees gigabytes of SSD space immediately and improves privacy without affecting Windows updates.
manualSteps: Open Terminal as Administrator and run: net stop DiagTrack
Open C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Diagnosis\ETLLogs and delete old AutoLogger and ETL files.
Restart the service with: net start DiagTrack

name: Windows Speech Recognition & Voice Dictation Model Cache
whatIsIt: Windows stores local acoustic language models, voice dictation profiles, and speech synthesizer cache files in %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Speech.
whatHappens: Safely frees disk space from unused speech profiles; active Windows 11 voice typing automatically re-downloads needed language assets.
manualSteps: Open %localappdata%\Microsoft in File Explorer.
Open the Speech folder and delete old audio training profiles and cache files.

name: Windows Remote Desktop (RDP) Bitmap Cache
whatIsIt: The Remote Desktop Connection client caches screen tiles and graphical bitmaps (bcache*.bmc files) to speed up remote session rendering.
whatHappens: Deleting the bitmap cache frees disk space and fixes corrupted graphics or black tiles in Remote Desktop sessions.
manualSteps: Close all active Remote Desktop Connection sessions.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache, and hit Enter.
Delete all .bmc and .bin files inside.

name: Windows Ink Workspace & Handwriting Personalization Cache
whatIsIt: Windows stores touch keyboard dictionary customizations, stylus handwriting samples, and ink strokes in InputPersonalization.
whatHappens: Safely frees storage space and resolves stylus lag or touch keyboard dictionary sync issues.
manualSteps: Open File Explorer and navigate to %localappdata%\Microsoft\InputPersonalization.
Delete temporary handwriting learning cache files.

name: Windows Action Center Notification History Database
whatIsIt: Windows maintains a local SQLite database (wpnidm / appcache.db) storing notification toasts, badge icons, and quick actions.
whatHappens: Safely shrinks bloated notification databases and fixes stuck, phantom, or repeating notification toasts.
manualSteps: Open Task Manager and end the Windows Explorer task.
Open Terminal (Admin) and delete %LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Notifications\wpnidm.sqlite.
Start explorer.exe to reinitialize a clean notification database.

name: Windows DISM Servicing Scratch Directory (%WINDIR%\Temp\DISM)
whatIsIt: When running DISM or system image repair operations, Windows mounts WIM images and stages uncompressed packages in Temp\DISM.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up abandoned mount points and orphaned scratch files left behind after interrupted servicing tasks.
manualSteps: Open Terminal as Administrator.
Run: dism /cleanup-wim to unmount any leftover servicing images.
Open C:\Windows\Temp\DISM and delete leftover scratch directories.

name: Garena PC Gaming Client Download Cache & Update Temp
whatIsIt: Garena caches game patches, news feeds, embedded browser assets, and download chunks inside %LocalAppData%\Garena\Cache.
whatHappens: Safely cleans up stale game update files and reclaims disk space without affecting installed games like Free Fire PC or League.
manualSteps: Exit the Garena PC client completely.
Press Windows Key + R, type %localappdata%\Garena\Cache, and press Enter.
Select and delete all files inside the cache folder.

name: Affinity Photo & Designer Scratch Disk Temp Files
whatIsIt: Serif Affinity Photo and Designer write scratch swap files and raster rendering buffers when working with high-resolution documents.
whatHappens: Safely deletes leftover swap files from closed sessions, freeing gigabytes of SSD space.
manualSteps: Close all Serif Affinity applications.
Open %localappdata%\Serif\Affinity in File Explorer.
Navigate to the Temp folder and delete lingering temporary swap files.

name: Inkscape Vector Graphics Thumbnail & Font Cache
whatIsIt: Inkscape caches SVG preview thumbnails, font metrics, and extension manifests inside %AppData%\inkscape\cache.
whatHappens: Frees disk space and fixes corrupted font listings or slow Inkscape startup times without touching your SVG designs.
manualSteps: Close Inkscape.
Open %appdata%\inkscape\cache in File Explorer.
Delete the cached thumbnail and font index files.

name: Maxon Cinema 4D Simulation & Viewport Render Cache
whatIsIt: Maxon Cinema 4D stores physics simulation caches, Redshift material previews, and viewport shader caches on your C: drive.
whatHappens: Reclaims significant disk space from old project renders without modifying your .c4d project files.
manualSteps: Exit Cinema 4D and Maxon App.
Navigate to %appdata%\Maxon in File Explorer.
Delete temporary simulation and thumbnail caches.

name: Clip Studio Paint Backup Canvas & Auto-Recovery Cache
whatIsIt: Clip Studio Paint writes autosave snapshots, material download archives, and canvas recovery states into CELSYS AppData.
whatHappens: Clears old recovery clutter and frees gigabytes of storage once your artwork is saved and backed up.
manualSteps: Save all active illustrations and exit Clip Studio Paint.
Open %appdata%\CELSYS in File Explorer.
Navigate to the DocumentBackup folder and clear obsolete autosaved files.
